subject: StratusSync connector: request for subprocessor lineage and DPA amendment
messages:
From: Ava Delgado <ava.delgado@stratussync.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratussync.com
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 11:14:00 -04:00
Subject: Request: subprocessor lineage + DPA amendment for StratusSync connector

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we get towards legal review for the StratusSync <> Redwood connector, our security team asked for a few specific items so we can finish our DPA amendment and sign-off:

- A current list of all subprocessors that will process StratusSync customer data when the connector is enabled (include country of processing and whether the vendor has access to plaintext).
- A short lineage map describing where logs, telemetry, and model inference traces flow (S3 buckets, third-party observability, any transit relays).
- Any planned changes in the next 90 days (temporary bridges, rollout windows).

We realize some of this may be sensitive — if possible, please send a redacted inventory and an attestation statement we can include in the DPA amendment. If there are standard artifacts (SOC2 evidence pointers, KMS locations) that you can share, that will speed our review.

Goal: legal wants to have the DPA amendment draft to procurement by next Wednesday (2028-05-17).

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Ava Delgado
Head of Integrations | StratusSync
[a] +1 415 555 0192

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor lineage + DPA amendment for StratusSync connector

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the clear list. We're able to provide a redacted subprocessor inventory and a short lineage summary. A couple of quick clarifying Qs before we prepare the package:

1) For "access to plaintext": do you want us to mark only those subprocessors that can access customer unencrypted content (e.g., for support or re-ingest)?
2) For the lineage map, do you prefer a simple table (component -> destination) or a visual diagram? We can provide both, but I want to match the format your legal team expects.

I'll route this to Legal and Security to assemble evidence pointers (SOC2 report links, KMS boundary notes). Kimberly, Marcus — can you weigh in on the suggested redaction level and whether we should include a temporary-bridge carveout note?

Targeting an initial packet by EOD Thursday (2028-05-16) so you have time to circulate.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Privacy Manager | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com | +1 650 555 2233

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 10:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor lineage + DPA amendment for StratusSync connector

Sofia —

Quick guidance from Legal:

- "Access to plaintext" should be flagged for subprocessors with technical or support access to customer content in cleartext. Mark as YES/NO; add a short justification column (e.g., "support ticket replays" or "inference cache for latency").
- Provide country of data processing per vendor and whether data is replicated to any other region. If onshore fallback exists, note that as well.
- For evidence, attach SOC2 report pointers where available and include HSM/KMS domain names (redact exact key IDs).

On redaction: redact IPs and exact bucket names; it's OK to give bucket logical names (e.g., "logs-prod-us-east-1"). Do not include internal incident timelines or unredacted support transcripts.

Operational note: Marcus, please confirm if the telemetry relay (EdgeRelayX) will be in-scope for StratusSync (I believe yes, with no plaintext access). If Marcus confirms, we'll prepare an attestation line for the DPA amendment and draft a single-paragraph addendum.

Marissa, can you prepare the initial inventory CSV with the required columns so Sofia can sign off on redactions?

Thanks —
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ava Delgado <ava.delgado@stratussync.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor lineage + DPA amendment for StratusSync connector

Hi Ava —

Appended is the initial packet we discussed. Per legal and security guidance it's redacted to remove exact buckets and key IDs but includes:

- A redacted subprocessor inventory (attached PDF) listing vendor, country(ies) of processing, access-to-plaintext flag, role (e.g., logging, inference, telemetry), and short justification.
- A CSV index of evidence pointers (SOC2 links, attestations).

Summary highlights:
- EdgeRelayX (US) — telemetry relay — NO plaintext access, replicated logs to us-east-1 for observability.
- InferenceCacheCo (US, EU) — inference cache; YES plaintext access for ephemeral caching to meet latency SLA.
- StoragePartner (US) — long-term logs archive; NO plaintext access (logs are encrypted at rest).

Next steps:
1) If this format works, Kimberly will prepare a one-paragraph DPA amendment attestation referencing the attached inventory.
2) We can redline the DPA amendment draft and route it to procurement.
3) If you need additional evidence (SOC2 report PDF), we can provide secure links under an NDA.

Attachments included: redwood_subprocessor_inventory_summary.pdf; subprocessor_evidence_index.csv; draft DPA amendment (for internal review). Also including a DocuSign link for the amendment when ready: https://docusign.com/yr9Xv9/subprocessor-amend-STRATUS

Let me know if you want a short call tomorrow morning (we're in PDT).

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Privacy Manager | Redwood Inference
